Negative-binomial recruit draw without the recruitment floor

Source: R/utils.R
rnbinom_torch_refined.Rd

The default regeneration sampler since 0.2.0, selected with createProcess(regeneration_sampler = "refined"); rnbinom_torch() (regeneration_sampler = "gaussian") reproduces results published before 0.2.0. Three differences: the probability clamp is 1e-10 instead of 1e-4, the Gamma draw is clamped at that same eps instead of taking +0.001 and an absolute value, and the draw goes through sample_poisson_refined() (an exact torch_poisson below lambda = 2, the Gaussian approximation above) instead of sample_poisson_gaussian().

Usage

rnbinom_torch_refined(pred, theta)

Arguments

pred

torch.Tensor Expected recruits per patch.

theta

torch.Tensor Negative-binomial dispersion.

Value

A torch tensor of recruit counts, of the shape of pred.

Details

The +0.001 offset and the 1e-4 clamp exist for the Gaussian branch: they keep the Gamma draw off zero and stop log(0) sending a NaN gradient back through distr_gamma()$rsample(). Neither hazard applies to torch_poisson, and together they impose a recruitment FLOOR of 0.0011 per cell-year, which at a FINN patch of 0.0168 ha is 0.066 recruits ha^-1 yr^-1 per species – over a pool of a hundred-odd species, as large as the whole ingrowth a temperate inventory records. sample_poisson_gaussian() (lambda + eps*sqrt(lambda), rounded straight-through by the forward pass) rounds the floor away but also rounds the signal away: at a FINN patch of 0.0168 ha the per-cell mean is 0.001-0.008, and over 2e6 draws the delivered fraction of the calibrated mean was 0.000-0.048 at theta = 1.

One bias is left and is not repaired in 0.2.0: above lambda = 2 the draw is the Gaussian approximation FLOORED, so it delivers about half a recruit per draw too few (measured over 1e6 draws: -0.43 at lambda = 2.5, -0.50 from lambda = 20, against about 0 with rounding). It bites only where a cell's mean recruitment is above two, which the per-patch means above are not. Rounding instead of flooring is planned for 0.2.1; it changes results, so it is not in this release.

For the measured consequence of both repairs on the simulated stand, and why the holdout cannot separate them, see binomial_from_poisson().

See also

recruitment, createProcess() (regeneration_sampler, theta_floor)

Examples

FINN.seed(1)
# sparse recruitment: an expected 0.05 recruits per patch and year
mu    <- torch::torch_full(c(100000), 0.05)
theta <- torch::torch_tensor(1)
r <- as.numeric(rnbinom_torch_refined(mu, theta))
mean(r)    # the draw delivers the expected count ...
#> [1] 0.05034
table(r)   # ... as whole recruits, most patches getting none
#> r
#>     0     1     2     3 
#> 95213  4548   231     8
